aboutMore: things i have ACTUALLY fixed (with my real hands, not the mainframe): my grandma's computer (a toolbar named Steve, she asked me to keep him, he lives in a folder now), mrs. abernathy's printer next door (the cat was in the tray), my dad's work laptop (it was 61 screensavers), and our router twice, after my mom unplugged it at 10 and then forgot where the cable went. i don't charge. mrs. abernathy pays me in lemon bars. best salary in the industry. i wouldn't call it hacking. it's closer to being a doctor for beige boxes. a doctor who also holds the flashlight.

blog.title: field guide: is ur computer sick? (a checklist for normal people)
blog.body: i get asked this about 3 times a week so here it is in writing. ur computer is sick if: 1) ur homepage changed to a site that sells watches. 2) a gorilla talks to u (larry, i'm looking at u, i'm looking at the Beast). 3) the little clock in the corner is off by a week. 4) there's a toolbar on ur toolbar. 5) it takes 14 minutes to boot and u have a theory about why. ur computer is NOT sick if: it's slow on a hot day (dust, blow on it, gently), the mouse is stuck (it's the ball, take it out, there's a little carpet in there), or the screen is black (check the cable. it's the cable. i'd say 97% of cases. 2% is the toolbar. 1% is something i have to read about at 2am and then enjoy). step 6: don't panic. step 7: call me. it's free. i'm up. (this is not sad it's tactical)

blog.title: my dad and the basement ceiling (a story about cable)
blog.body: when i was 12 i asked my dad how the internet got into the basement. he's a lineman for the electric company so he didn't answer, he went and got a roll of blue cable and a crimper and said 'hold this.' we ran it through the ceiling over one whole saturday. he asked what the load was going to be. i said 'a game of counter strike.' he said 'then we over-build it,' and he did, about 4 times what it needed. he made me put masking tape on both ends of every cable and write where it goes. his rule: if you can't find the other end in the dark, the job isn't done. there are 11 jacks in our house. 9 go nowhere. my mom calls them decorations. my dad calls them 'for later.' i have never told him i don't totally know what i do on the computer. he has never asked. he just holds the flashlight. sometimes for 3 hours. i think that's the harder job.

blog.title: mr henderson's newt has a temperature log now
blog.body: so mr henderson (science, room 114) asked if i could 'make the computer in the corner stop saying a thing.' the thing was a pop-up. it was the only pop-up. he'd been closing it since august like a man bailing out a boat. fixed in 4 minutes. while i was in there i noticed his grade file was called PASSWORDS_DO_NOT_OPEN and his login was SirIsaacNewt1. i did NOT open the file. i sat him down and explained, calmly, with a diagram. he took it very well. he wrote DAVE: IT on the whiteboard in green pen (he says red is aggressive). then i hooked a little thermometer to the newt's tank and now there is a log. sir isaac newt: 71 degrees. 71 degrees. 71.4. he gave me a granola bar. i have never felt more like a professional. security level: maximum. (the newt is fine) (the newt does not care)

blog.title: THE BLACKOUT LAN (an after-action report)
blog.body: attendance: 6 (mom's rule). wes (2 CRTs), josh, kevin (a sweatband and 4 energy drinks, the 4th at 8:58 which is a violation), a kid from down the street named pete, my cousin who doesn't play but wanted to see, and me. at 8:12 i plugged in the 7th monitor and the entire basement went dark. i had run 6 towers, 2 CRTs, a lava lamp and a space heater (not mine) off one outlet. we sat there for 14 minutes. nobody spoke. then wes said very quietly 'frame data' and we laughed so hard my mom came downstairs with a flashlight and pizza rolls. we played charades by flashlight. wes did the matrix. it looked exactly like melee. kevin did 'butterfly' with his feet. josh got it. best LAN i've ever hosted. i'm logging it as SUCCESSFUL (power: no).

74 wpm. 61 if somebody is watching

one that turned every icon on my desktop into a lizard. i left it 3 days. i got attached. (the lizard. he was a nice lizard)
what's on ur desktop:
one folder called taxes. it's not taxes. it's also not what u think. it's wallpapers

ctrl+z. it's the closest thing to a time machine most people will ever own. i give it a moment of silence on sundays

nobody. i'm the number. my grandma has me in her phone as 'computer grandson' (i'm her only grandson) (still)

my first batch file. 3 lines. it says hello and then closes. i think about it a lot

hold the router like a baby bird and listen to 11 machines not running. security is also physical

a room with no windows (glare) and one window (the sun) and a snack drawer. i know that doesn't work. i'm working on it
describe urself in one sentence:
i could hack the site but i would rather fix your printer
